items.title: 15 Best Open World Games on PS5 You Need to Play
items.summary: Explore the best open world games on PS5, from Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077 to Spider-Man 2 and Horizon Forbidden West.
items.content:
Open-world games are easy to lose yourself in because they let you decide what happens next. You can follow the story or clear side quests. You can also head in the opposite direction because something in the distance caught your attention. On PS5, that can mean anything from exploring the Lands Between in Elden Ring to swinging across New York in Marvel’s Spider-Man 2.

Some games also benefit from faster loading, performance modes, and DualSense features. At the same time, backward compatibility keeps some of the PS4 generation’s best open worlds in the mix. Red Dead Redemption 2 is a perfect example.

For our list of the best open world games on PS5, I looked at world design, exploration, and overall immersion. I also wanted a mix of newer releases and games that have held up over time. The result covers fantasy, sci-fi, historical settings, RPGs, city sandboxes, and a few open worlds that do things very differently.

If you’re still deciding which PlayStation 5 to buy, our PS5 buying guide breaks down the differences between the models. Here, we’re looking at the worlds you’ll want to explore once you start playing.

A big map doesn’t automatically make a great open world. What matters is whether you want to see what’s over the next hill or down the next street. Maybe it’s a path you almost walked past.

The best open worlds let curiosity take over. You might spot ruins in the distance, run into a side story, or leave the road because something nearby looks interesting.

That’s when exploration becomes part of the adventure instead of a list of icons to clear. Hidden areas, optional quests, secrets, and unexpected encounters all play a part.

A memorable world also needs its own personality. That can come from the people living there, the weather, architecture, music, wildlife, or simply the way different areas look and sound.

Red Dead Redemption 2 gets there through believable routines and chance encounters. Cyberpunk 2077 goes the other way, filling Night City with lights, crowds, traffic, businesses, and activity almost everywhere you turn.

It also feels better to explore when your character changes along the way. New abilities, gear, skill trees, and traversal options can alter how you deal with areas you’ve already seen.

Sometimes that means returning to a place that was too dangerous earlier. Other times, a new ability opens a route you couldn’t reach before.

Elden Ring drops you into the Lands Between with very little direction, turning every detour into your own discovery.

Ghost of Tsushima Director’s Cut lets Tsushima guide you, with the Guiding Wind replacing a constant navigation marker.

Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 turns traversal into part of the adventure. Swinging and gliding across New York rarely gets old.

items.title: 5 Best Video Games Like Star Wars Outlaws
items.summary: Setting aside the divided response, "Star Wars Outlaws" offered a new way to explore the galaxy far, far away. These five games offer similar freedom.
items.content:
Ubisoft Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The Star Wars franchise has bounced back in a major way in the video game industry in recent years, with releases such as "Jedi Fallen Order" and "Zero Company" receiving rave reviews from critics and fans alike. However, the community is still divided over "Star Wars Outlaws," which continues to collect mixed reviews now up to two years after its release. Even if it's not your favorite Star Wars game, though, "Outlaws" does possess some enjoyable qualities that you can often find in other games.

Whether it's the feeling of playing through one of our pop culture's most iconic franchises or just experiencing the various mechanics featured in "Outlaws," there's plenty to like about the open-world game. Of course, if you've already played through "Outlaws" once, you might be looking for a similar experience in a fresher-to-you game. If you fall into that crowd, then you can keep reading below for five games that are very similar to "Star Wars Outlaws" in multiple ways.

Ubisoft It feels right to start this list off with another game in the Star Wars universe, and why not run with another polarizing entry in the franchise? "Star Wars Jedi: Survivor" is the sequel to "Jedi: Fallen Order," which, put together, are two of the best "Star Wars" games ever . The second game continues the adventures of rebel Cal Kestis, still ducking those who would erase the remaining Jedi. "Survivor" is set between the events of Episode III and Episode IV in the Star Wars timeline, so there are plenty of recognizable characters alive and well in the galaxy.

Compared to "Outlaws," "Jedi: Survivor" features more challenging combat, less open exploration, and more of an emphasis on the narrative than on RPG mechanics. However, it still offers plenty of what you might have liked from "Outlaws," as you get to explore several iconic planets, solve complex puzzles, and experience a thrill ride of a story with twists and turns you'll never see coming. If you happen to like this series as well, then make sure to also check out the best games like "Star Wars Jedi."

CD Projekt Red The setting of any Star Wars game has always been one of the most alluring parts of the franchise, with the sci-fi elements always taking center stage. Well, while it's not quite set in a galaxy far, far away, "Cyberpunk 2077" is easily one of the best sci-fi games of the modern era. Set in the year 2077, it offers a beautiful and dystopian look at the United States where technology and AI have completely transformed everyday life, but at a steep cost to individual identity.

"Cyberpunk 2077" is also heralded as a top RPG in the genre, featuring a massive skill tree of abilities and multiple different character builds that completely change the way you play the game. While this differs from "Star Wars Outlaws," which is more of an action-adventure game, "Cyberpunk 2077" still offers fantastic open-world exploration, unique ways to traverse the world, and a story that will keep you busy for dozens of hours.

Guerrilla Games "Horizon Zero Dawn" offers one of the more comparable experiences to "Star Wars Outlaws," especially in that both are open-world action-adventure games that center around a female protagonist who has the world set against her. In "Horizon Zero Dawn," you play as Aloy, an outcast who was born one thousand years in the future after a technological post-apocalypse ravaged the United States — and the world. To put it mildly.

The primary cause behind the apocalypse is a greedy technology CEO, Ted Faro, who created AI machines designed for militaristic purposes. However, the AI in the machines grew smarter and more corrupt over time, leading them to self-replicate and overthrow humanity as the dominant species on Earth. The AI machines, which may look like a variety of real animals, still roam the Earth and keep human civilizations in a permanent, prehistoric state during the main story. The open-world exploration and the lore behind the events that led to the story in "Horizon Zero Dawn" are its two standout features, similar to "Outlaws," but the unique combat that you can customize through different weapons and skills is also a highly enjoyable part of the game.

Obsidian Entertainment If you were hoping that "Star Wars Outlaws" would have more RPG mechanics, then "Avowed" should be right up your alley. Developed by Obsidian Entertainment, the team behind "Fallout: New Vegas" and "The Outer Worlds," "Avowed" is an RPG through and through, allowing you to create a character and custom-build them with skills and abilities. You'll also have the opportunity to make narrative choices that completely alter your character's ending.

However, aside from the RPG part of the game, "Avowed" features a map that has several distinct open zones, similar to how the planets are structured in "Outlaws." The story progresses as you complete the narrative elements in these zones, and each one offers different side quests, hub towns filled with NPCs, some of which you can recruit to your party, and unique environments. While "Avowed" doesn't really feel like "Outlaws" in a gameplay sense, it does offer a great story (built in Obsidian's own world, Eora, a fixture of their "Pillars of Eternity" franchise), open and varied exploration, and the ability to affect the world around your character.

Ubisoft Star Wars isn't the only massive entertainment franchise that started as a movie but eventually offered up a video game as well. "Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora" is the first video game set in the "Avatar" universe, which is comprised of three films so far. It actually surpassed the original Star Wars movies as the highest-grossing film trilogy of all time. While "Frontiers of Pandora" didn't break any records, it still stands as a terrific open-world action-adventure game that mirrors "Outlaws" in more ways than one.

Both games are set in iconic locations, with "Frontiers of Pandora" taking place on Pandora itself, and feature original stories from their respective universes. "Frontiers of Pandora" also allows you to freely traverse the world, using a wide variety of traversal options, combat mechanics, and skills to navigate the 20-hour story campaign. If you're looking to live out a dream in another iconic fantasy world, then "Frontiers of Pandora" is one you don't want to miss.

items.title: Brand-New Cyberpunk Game Hits Steam Store
items.summary: The cyberpunk genre expands with a brand-new game available now on Steam that offers an unexpected twist to the typical sci-fi formula.
items.content:
Brand-New Cyberpunk Game Hits Steam Store From GameRant (Written by Charming Holiday) on October 6, 2026 | OpenCritic

Fans of the cyberpunk genre have a brand-new futuristic life-sim RPG to dive into with Nivalis Nights . While a notable chunk of entries in the genre carry certain expectations of violence and drama, Nivalis Nights reminds audiences that not all sci-fi games have to be nightmarish dystopias. Ironically, the game also highlights the often overlooked instance of cozy games not always wearing a cottagecore veil, offering a unique new take on the cyberpunk formula.

Serving as an indirect sequel to the hit 2020 open-world sci-fi PC game Cloudpunk , Nivalis Nights once again transports players into a neon-soaked world highly reminiscent of cities seen in games like Cyberpunk 2077 . However, Nivalis Nights sets itself apart from its contemporaries by following in the footsteps of its predecessor. Its surprisingly cozy slice-of-life approach promises a swaying pendulum between easy-going and high intensity, both in its overall approach to storytelling and world-building, driven largely by the prioritization of player choice.

This new Steam sci-fi metroidvania feels like Ori meets Outer Wilds, but one twist makes its familiar progression loop feel surprisingly dated.

items.title: "We opted out of some things really early on": How the small team making No Law plan to make it look as big as Cyberpunk 2077
items.summary: Open-world sci-fi RPG No Law looks like it could rival Cyberpunk 2077, but the developers have found clever ways to make it seem bigger than it is
items.content:
Image credit: Krafton / Neon Giant Feature by Julian Benson Editorial Director Published on Oct. 5, 2026, 8:30 a.m. 10 comments Follow No Law If you've watched the trailers for No Law or the tech demo that developer Neon Giant showed off at Unreal Fest earlier this year, it would be easy to believe the game has a similar scope to CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077 . After all, both games are open-world RPGs set in cyberpunk cities. Set in a beautifully realised mediterranean city that is somehow equal parts Lisbon and Kowloon Walled City – and with corner shops that are as stuffed with riches as the one down the road from my flat . But, the developers will happily tell you where they've scrimped and saved.

First thing on the table: Neon Giant are not as big as CD Project Red. One of No Law's creative directors, Tor Frick told me there are just 24 people working on the game. Now that number doesn't include the outsourcing teams helping with QA, art, and sound design, but even then, this is a smaller production. (Also, it's hardly new for developers to talk about games in this way, as Nic pointed out around the release of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Still, Neon Giant knew their head count going into development and so it shaped a lot about the game that would become No Law.

"We picked a really, really difficult game to make, and we know that," Frick says. No Law is an open-world immersive sim in which you're trying to kill off the four mayors of Port Desire, a small coastal city policed by a peacekeeping force. The game is built of layered interlocking systems, allowing you to combine items to create new weaponry, like time-slowing grenades and remote exploding drones, you can approach each mission in a myriad of ways, and, as you kill off the mayors, the surviving magistrates will alter their patterns and defences to protect themselves against your rampage. And the world itself is fully open with no loading screens and many of its citizens have homes you can visit (and break into).

Essentially, it looks like too much of a game to be made by 24 people. Even if it was actually made by slightly more than that, that's still wildly ambitious. However, as with any creative pursuit, Neon Giant recognised their limitations and designed them into the game.

"We opted out of some things really early on," Frick explains, pointing out that while you can see cars parked on the street, you won't be driving any of them. That both saves the team having to build out that functionality but it also reveals something about Port Desire's open world: "This is a city that is built to be navigated on foot," he says.

The land mass of Port Desire is significantly smaller than Cyberpunk 2077's Night City. Where that city sprawls out across multiple city-sized districts, Neon Giant keeps Port Desire tight, instead leaning into verticality. This is a city made up of tall tower blocks and steep hills. You are forever climbing and descending, moving over, under, and through buildings, which gives you the impression of a much larger area than its footprint would suggest. "We really want the player to be distracted and explore things," Frick says, saying they wanted to capture the feeling of being in the winding streets of a Mediterranean city where you might turn a corner and find a little alley or a staircase leading you up or down unexpectedly – "We wanted the sense of discovery as you move through the city," he says.

They also nixed other ideas early on that would have become too much work, like being able to enter every building. "We try to focus it in areas that feel natural for the player to explore," Frick says. Still, to give you that sense of density, you can enter some buildings, such as understreet night clubs, sleazy bars in the red light district, or apartments where characters you can find in the city live.

Though, as Neon Giant wanted to avoid any loading screens, that created its own limitation on how they build environments. "Every physical space exists as it should, so interiors of buildings match the exterior," Frick explains. "It's not like going into a loading screen and the building is much bigger on the inside."

The process of picking constraints, as often happens, led to creativity. The necessity for a small dense city came before the narrative reasons for it existing. "It was very important for us that we don't have invisible walls, so that's why the city is surrounded by deep seas and a border wall," Frick says. That led to the narrative setting inspired by Kowloon Walled City. "This is a lawless city set between three neighbouring countries – like no man's land," he adds. "There's no invisible walls, there's just very visible walls. And then we have populated it with the mission locations in areas where it makes sense."

For the systems the team did choose to add in, Neon Giant are trying to make sure they thread through the world and change how the game plays – "We want all those layers to contribute so that people have different experiences," Frick says.

Frick uses the time and weather as an example. Time passes naturally in No Law and its weather changes, both of which have implications as you're playing. "Different districts will have different populations and characters based on the time of day and weather," Frick says. "When it's smoggy, almost no one goes outside. If it's rainy, down in the party area, it doesn't matter: it's still full of people. But the residential area people keep inside. Night time in the slums, no one goes out at night. Night time in the bazaar, it's full of people." While this adds realism to the city, it also has an impact on your missions. If you need to break into a building on a busy street, you can do it in the daytime, but if you wait until night, it may well be easier.

Talk to any developer about how they made their game, and you'll quickly learn they're really just made of paper and the hope that players don't look at anything too closely . We all remember Fallout's train hat… . So No Law is not unique in that regard, but for a game that is so expansive, it's interesting to learn where it's actually smaller than it appears.

Travel and accommodation to Gamescom was provided by the conference organisers.

items.title: New cyberpunk game with "miserable" performance hit by negative Steam reviews, dev says just 'restart the game'
items.summary: Nivalis Nights is the latest title from ION LANDS and 505 Games, but its optimization so far leaves a lot to be desired, players say.
items.content:
Last Updated on September 30, 2026 PC Guide is reader-supported. When you buy through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Read More Table of Contents Nivalis Nights performance issues are the game’s main downside Prime Day is here! We've found all the biggest and best deals from this year's event below. The newly released Nivalis Nights, developed by ION LANDS and published by 505 Games, may have gone under the radar for many people given the big The Witcher 3 Remastered patch yesterday (which is facing its own performance criticisms ), but the new cyberpunk-themed title has its own optimization worries, even on high-end hardware.

Even a positive review in which a user praises Nivalis Nights as “one of the coolest games I’ve ever seen” admits that the performance is “miserable” despite running it on an RTX 4090 & i9-12900KS combo. The developer’s response from 505 Games comes with a copy-and-paste statement that suggests restarting the game or switching your PC’s power mode.

It’s worth pointing out that the game still holds a Mostly Positive review rating at the time of writing, but we notice that many of them touch on performance issues despite the final thumbs-up verdict. The developer says “frame rate can vary in areas with lots of NPCs,” but doesn’t really offer any proper solution outside of restarting the game or relying on a pretty basic power mode setting change.

Many players so far have mentioned Cyberpunk 2077 in their reviews so far, for good and bad reasons. Nivalis Nights’ atmosphere is being widely praised thanks to its cyberpunk setting, but it’s also being scorched for its performance. As seen in the review above, it reportedly runs worse than CP2077 on its top ‘Psycho’ ray-tracing setting.

“I actually have higher FPS in CP2077 with path tracing on than in this game when looking somewhere with more than 5 NPCs,” says one review , highlighting the issue mentioned by the developer in relation to the more NPC-heavy areas. That’s with an RTX 5070 GPU and 5700X3D CPU. For now, it seems players will simply have to wait for optimization updates.

Nivalis Nights is a completely different genre from CD Projekt Red’s ambitious ARPG. Instead, it’s a life simulator game with a more relaxing vibe to it. “It’s really scratched that Cyberpunk itch,” says one reviewer ; “This is exactly the kind of cyberpunk game I have been waiting for,” says another . So while the gameplay and atmosphere are great, its performance leaves a lot to be desired.

Would you buy a cheaper version of the Steam Frame that doesn’t work standalone?

Yes, as long as the price is significantly lower ($750 or less)

items.title: No Law might be the open-world Deus Ex that Cyberpunk 2077 wasn't
items.content:
CD Projekt's sci-fi RPG was close to being my perfect game. But it fell short in one specific area.

Also like many people, I think CD Projekt did a superb job fixing it. Post- Phantom Liberty Cyberpunk is one of my favourite games, to the point where I might just love it even more than The Witcher 3.

That said, even in its superior modern form, Cyberpunk isn't quite the game that I wish it was—namely an open world Deus Ex . CD Projekt's early trailers and gameplay demos implied a more immersive sim-like experience, and there are many elements in the final game that are immersive sim-like. The range of abilities it offers, the mixture of stealth and combat, the playful, mischievous hacking skills, the side-missions that often let you infiltrate or attack a compound from multiple angles of approach. It's all the kind of stuff you'd expect to see in a Deus Ex game with the scope blown out.

Ultimately, though, Cyberpunk 2077 isn't that game. Your progress and prowess is far too tightly bound to your character level to make it a functioning immersive sim. Plugging points into skill trees will transform mechanics like stealth from next to useless to being massively overpowered. And those open-ended missions are very much a side dish. Whenever the central storyline rears its head, Cyberpunk becomes as linear and prescribed as a Call of Duty campaign.

Whenever the central storyline rears its head, Cyberpunk becomes as linear and prescribed as a Call of Duty campaign.

To be clear, I'm not complaining—I've come to love Cyberpunk just the way it is. But I would still love to play the Cyberpunk that exists in my head, even if it's just to see whether it would actually work. And that's why I'm so intrigued by No Law, because it looks a whole lot like the Cyberpunk that I erroneously imagined.

No Law is the new game from Neon Giant, creators of the gleefully grimy cyberpunk twin-stick shooter The Ascent . No Law maintains the cyberpunk theme but is otherwise a completely different style of game. Taking place in a city called Port Desire, No Law sees you play as Grey Harker, an archetypal military veteran who is dragged reluctantly away from a newfound life of peace after (and Neon Giant has kept this bit vague) trouble comes knocking at his door.

Tokyo Walled City looks set to fill the Deus Ex-shaped hole in my life Dishonored director Harvey Smith thinks there's still room for big-budget immersive sims: 'When it really comes together and it has the budget behind it and the team, you end up with Deus Ex or Dishonored' The latest ugly-cool immersive sim is scratching my itch for new Deus Ex

Neon Giant describes No Law as a "first-person open world shooter RPG". That's often what developers say when they're planning to make an immersive sim, but don't want to use the phrase because nobody under 35 knows what an immersive sim is. However, that's also how CD Projekt described Cyberpunk prior to release, and that turned out not to be an immersive sim, so it's by no means guaranteed.

That said, I've got a good feeling that No Law might be what Cyberpunk wasn't, at least going by Neon Giant have shown of (and said about) the game thus far. No Law's most recent trailer , which debuted at Gamescom's Opening Night Live, went to considerable length to emphasise the variety of approaches that Harker can take during missions.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Inevitably, shooting enemies in the face is one possible approach. But you also see Harker sneaking through vents, stealth-killing guards and using some weird sci-fi abilities. One of these makes enemies' heads explode, while another makes their entire bodies burst like balloons. I'm also impressed by Harker's mighty kick, which he uses to boot doors off hinges and enemies off their mortal coils. It brings back fond memories of punting enemies off ledges and down staircases in Deathloop and Dark Messiah: Might and Magic .

By far my favourite moment in the trailer, however, is when Harker attaches a grenade to a laptop-shaped Roomba, assumes control of it, and then pilots it into a garage filled with guards where it detonates. That's the kind of kooky, indirect solution to a problem any Deus Ex game would be proud to feature.

items.summary: I would never want to tell our story that way
items.content:
"I would never want to tell our story that way"

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Cyberpunk 2077 's redemption arc is long complete, 2023's acclaimed Phantom Liberty expansion cementing the RPG's legacy as one of this generation's all-time greats. Even as I sit here in 2026 writing this, it's still jarring to talk about Cyberpunk 2077 in such a uniformly positive light, and that's because I was doing this exact same job back in December 2020 when the game finally launched after multiple delays... and got absolutely dragged through the mud. We have a curated list of the best Cyberpunk 2077 bugs we could find at the time, if that gives you an idea of the state of the game at launch.

Shortly after launch, developer CD Projekt Red began rapid firing patches and updates at Cyberpunk 2077 in an effort to address widespread performance and technical issues, culminating in the massive 1.5 "next-gen" update that really marked a turning point in the game's overall trajectory. The whole Edgerunners update and Netflix tie-in sealed the deal, and Phantom Liberty felt like icing on the cake. Cyberpunk 2077 was back, baby. And yet, its initial launch was so disastrous that it'll forever remain a scar on CDPR's resume, a fact not lost on designer Pawel Sasko.

Reflecting on three years of Phantom Liberty in a lengthy Twitter post , Sasko says: "I do not think Phantom Liberty erases the launch of Cyberpunk 2077, and I would never want to tell our story that way." I have a feeling there's a part of every person working at CDPR that wishes things were handled differently at Cyberpunk 2077's launch, but I admire Sasko's acknowledgment of the very real issues paying customers like myself faced six years ago.

"Phantom Liberty sold more than 15 million copies by now. I am incredibly grateful for those numbers, but what stays with me most after three years is what making this expansion taught me about directing games, trusting people, making choices meaningful, giving characters space to breathe and accepting the scars that come with making something this difficult," he writes.

Not to beat a previously dead horse, but Cyberpunk 2077's launch wasn't just a technical mess. It was a full-blown disaster, prompting several storefronts to offer refunds and Sony to issue a warning on the PlayStation Store not to buy the game on PS4. Yes, Phantom Liberty is great, and yes, it absolutely does not "erase the launch of Cyberpunk 2077."

Boot up your rig and jack in, chooms! Cyberpunk 2077 is now available on Xbox Game Pass Premium and Ultimate for Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One!

It's a perfect opportunity to visit Night City for the first time or come back for one more run ;)

Available now on the official Xbox Store: https://cp2077.ly/XboxGamePass

items.title: Coming to Xbox Game Pass: Cyberpunk 2077, Planet of Lana II, and More
items.summary: Wake up samurai, we have games to play. Whether you want to check out haunted kingdoms, Night City, or the track, we have something for you. Here's what's coming soon to Xbox Game Pass!
items.content:
Wake up samurai, we have games to play. Whether you want to check out haunted kingdoms, Night City, or the track, we have something for you. Let’s get to the games!

Final Fantasy III (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass

With the power of light nearly eclipsed by the power of darkness, only the crystals’ four chosen adventurers can save the world.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance II (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass

Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is a thrilling Action RPG, set amid the chaos of a civil war in 15th Century Bohemia. You are Henry of Skalitz – an ordinary man doing extraordinary things – caught in a gripping tale of revenge, betrayal and discovery as he embarks on an epic journey.

to a T (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) – March 4 Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass

A charming, colorful adventure game from the creator of Katamari Damacy and the uvula team about a teen navigating life in a small town with their cute dog companion. While their body is stuck in a T-pose, they do their best to make the most of it.

EA Sports F1 25 (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) – March 4 Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

Write your own legendary racing story, lead your team, and explore new modes in the official video game of the 2025 FIA Formula One World Championship. Game Pass Ultimate subscribers can play now with EA Play and grab this month’s 5,000 XP Boost, available until March 31.

Planet of Lana II: Children of the Leaf (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) – March 5 Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

Available day one with Xbox Game Pass! Can a friendship change the world? Embark on an unforgettable sci-fi adventure with Lana and her loyal companion Mui. Solve clever puzzles, uncover hidden secrets, and confront the dangers reshaping their home. This breathtaking cinematic platformer is sure to challenge your mind, stir your heart, and dazzle your eyes and ears.

Construction Simulator (Cloud, Console, and PC) – March 10 Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass

Construction Simulator has returned – larger and more impressive than ever! Fulfil your ambition to become a successful construction entrepreneur by establishing your business from scratch, assisted by your mentor, Hape.

Cyberpunk 2077 (Cloud and Console) – March 10 Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium

items.title: It’s All About You! — Never Fade Away

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.

items.title: Patch 2.31
items.summary: Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live! This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below: Vehicles Updated Aut
items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

items.content:
Surviving the City of Dreams is tough, but a choom at your side can make all the difference.

In our latest It’s All About You episode, we’re celebrating all of our iconic duos living on the edge! Night City wouldn’t shine quite so bright without them. 

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners in the most creative ways possible. Don't forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY. See you in the next episode!

items.title: Update 2.3 Patch Notes
items.summary: Update 2.3 lands tomorrow! Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as sup
items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Color Balance tab, allowing you to create your own custom filters.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Time and Weather tab:

    • Weather: includes rain, acid rain, fog, sandstorm, pollution, and sunny.

      [/*]

    • Time of Day: changes the time of day within Photo Mode.

      [/*]

    • Frame Forward: advances through an unlimited amount of frames to capture the perfect shot.

      [/*]

    • Game Speed: allows in-game time to progress while in Photo Mode."

      [/*]
    [/*]

Quality of Life & Accessibility

  • The game will now detect if the player is using inverted mouse button settings and automatically adjusts in-game button prompts accordingly.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to toggle aiming down sights in Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Jobs & Open World

  • Cyberpsycho Sighting: Bloody Ritual - the "Crack the ritualist's shard" objective now properly disappears from the Journal after completing the objective.

    [/*]

  • Sex on Wheels - now properly appears in the Journal after receiving the message from Jake Estevez.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where selecting a specific dialogue option in the conversation with Bree created a nameless, iconless item in the player's Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where the button to go to the lower level didn't appear on the elevator panel.

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, when using a controller in Trauma Drama, the controllable character would default to shooting upwards instead of forward.

    [/*]

  • Players can now drop more Cyberware Capacity Shards if some within the intended drop limit were previously missed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing automatic weapons to fire slower than intended.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Official BARGHEST Tac Vest didn't drop from the scripted Airdrop as intended.

    [/*]

  • The level 60 Engineer perk no longer activates the EMP blast outside of combat or after entering a vehicle.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to replay the gameplay tutorial at any time via Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Added an option to tell Johnny to go away after you look at him for a short while when he appears in the passenger seat. He takes the hint and disappears as a passenger for a couple days.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the sound of V's Radioport could be randomly interrupted by the Radioports of nearby NPCs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where History by Gazelle Twin and Trash Generation played too loudly compared to other songs on the radio.

    [/*]

  • Improved the HDR Setting screen: fixed the HDR calibration preview so it correctly reflects the chosen settings, and clarified the description of the "Tone-Mapping Midpoint" setting.

    [/*]

  • Updated the End User Licence Agreement. You will be asked to accept it again when you load the game after updating.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several visual issues with missing, clipping, or floating textures.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several localization issues in various languages.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 for compatible AMD GPUs. IMPORTANT: The FSR 4 option will not be available in the in-game settings until the supporting AMD driver is installed. Please note that the driver will be released at a later date.

    [/*]

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution Frame Generation 3.1 for compatible hardware. It can now be used in combination with any upscaler.

    [/*]

  • Added support for ​Intel XeSS 2.0, with XeSS Frame Generation available on compatible hardware.

    [/*]

  • Added support for HDR10+ GAMING certified Intel GPUs. To enable this feature, your display must support the technology (find my display) and have "Game Mode" enabled. The HDR10+ GAMING toggle can be found in Settings in the Video tab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the DLSS Super Resolution Preset would invisibly revert from the CNN model to the Transformer model after restarting the game, even though the UI still displayed the CNN model as active.

    [/*]

  • Added more detailed information to the DLSS Super Resolution Preset tooltip in Settings to help players choose the best option for their setup.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to move the mouse cursor to a different display while in Windowed Borderless mode.

    [/*]

  • Increased the maximum save size from 12 MB to 15 MB.

    [/*]

  • It will now be possible to rebind the key used to jump out of vehicles with the Stuntjock perk.

    [/*]
